Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

huge adjective

also enormous, vast, immense, gigantic, massive

classical

Cic. Lael. 98, quoting Ter. Eun. 391–392
Verg. G. 2.412–413: laudātō ingentia rūra, exiguum colitō
Gell. 5.14.22: stirpem ingentem

ingēns, ingentis

adjective, third declension, one ending

huge, enormous, vast

Bigger than magnus: Cicero remarks that the flatterer in Terence, asked whether Thais thanks his master “greatly”, answers not magnās but ingentīs (Cic. Lael. 98).

Other words

  • immānis, immāne — monstrous, enormous

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 6.16: simulācra immānī magnitūdine (Lewis & Short)

    Huge and frightening.

  • immēnsus, immēnsa, immēnsum — immense, boundless

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 3.70: ingēns immēnsusque campus (Lewis & Short)

  • ēnormis, ēnorme — enormous, immense

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Tac. Agr. 10: spatium (Lewis & Short); Suet. Calig. 50: corpus (Lewis & Short)

    Post-Augustan: first “out of rule, irregular” (from norma; Quint. 11.3.139), then “immense” (Tac., Plin., Suet.; Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • ‘magnās vērō agere grātiās Thāis mihi?’ satis erat respondēre ‘magnās’. ‘ingentīs’ inquit. semper auget assentātor id, quod is, cujus ad voluntātem dīcitur, volt esse magnum

    ‘Is Thais really very grateful to me?’ It would have been enough to answer ‘very’; ‘hugely’, says he. The flatterer always makes bigger whatever the man he is pleasing wants to be bigCic. Lael. 98

  • laudātō ingentia rūra, exiguum colitō

    praise huge estates; farm a small oneVerg. G. 2.412–413

  • ego stirpem ingentem, vestīgiō pedis ejus haerentem, revellī

    I pulled out a huge thorn stuck in the sole of his pawGell. 5.14.22

See also big, giant, tiny.
